# Evaluating the Limit Using the Dominated Convergence Theorem

## Setting Up the Problem

Define the sequence of functions on $[1,\infty)$:

$$f_n(x) = \frac{x^{-2}}{\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}} = \frac{x^{-2}}{(1+x^{3n})^{1/n}}$$

## Finding the Pointwise Limit

For every $x \ge 1$, since $x^{3n} \ge 1$, I factor:

$$(1+x^{3n})^{1/n} = \left(x^{3n}(1+x^{-3n})\right)^{1/n} = x^3\left(1+x^{-3n}\right)^{1/n}$$

Since $0 < x^{-3n} \le 1$ for $x\ge 1$, we have $1 < 1+x^{-3n} \le 2$, so by the squeeze theorem:

$$\left(1+x^{-3n}\right)^{1/n} \le 2^{1/n} \to 1 \quad \text{as } n\to\infty$$

Therefore $(1+x^{3n})^{1/n} \to x^3$, and:

$$f_n(x) \;\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}\; \frac{x^{-2}}{x^3} = x^{-5}$$

## Applying the Dominated Convergence Theorem

**Domination:** For all $n$ and all $x \ge 1$:

$$1 + x^{3n} \ge x^{3n} \implies (1+x^{3n})^{1/n} \ge x^3$$

This gives the pointwise bound:

$$0 \le f_n(x) = \frac{x^{-2}}{(1+x^{3n})^{1/n}} \le \frac{x^{-2}}{x^3} = x^{-5} \equiv g(x)$$

**Integrability of the dominant:**

$$\int_1^{\infty} x^{-5}\,dx = \left[-\frac{1}{4x^4}\right]_1^{\infty} = \frac{1}{4} < \infty$$

So $g(x)=x^{-5}\in L^1([1,\infty))$, satisfying all hypotheses of the **Lebesgue Dominated Convergence Theorem**.

## Computing the Limit

By the DCT, I may interchange the limit and the integral:

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{[1,\infty)} \frac{x^{-2}}{\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}}\,d\lambda \;=\; \int_{[1,\infty)} \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{x^{-2}}{\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}}\,d\lambda \;=\; \int_1^{\infty} x^{-5}\,dx \;=\; \frac{1}{4}$$

## Conclusion

The limit **converges** to $\dfrac{1}{4}$.

$$\boxed{\dfrac{1}{4}}$$
